chunks: My father and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn and others narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khallid, from his father, from Harun ibn Jahm, from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said:

Al-'Ali, the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), passed by the graves and stood in the thoroughfare. Then he said to his right: 'Peace be upon you, O people of the graves, who have moved from palaces. You have preceded us and we are your followers, and indeed, if God wills, we shall join you.' Then he turned to his left and said: 'Peace be upon you, O people of the graves,' repeating the same statement until the end.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say when visiting the graves?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the ritualized etiquette of visiting graves, where Imam Ali (AS) stood in the center of the path to address the deceased directly, emphasizing the transient nature of worldly palaces versus the eternal abode of the grave. The phrase 'you are our vanguard and we are your followers' underscores the Shia concept of *Tabaqat* (stages) in the afterlife, reinforcing the hope for reunion (*Lihaq*) among the faithful. This practice establishes the theological basis for *Salat al-Mayyit* and the intercessory potential of the deceased for the living.
